name: Alien Employment Permit before a foreign national starts work

rules.description: Secure the DOLE Alien Employment Permit for a foreign national before the employment starts.
rules.authority: Labor Code art.40; DOLE Department Order 221-21: a non-resident foreign national may be employed only with an Alien Employment Permit issued before work starts. Recorded default: a profile `nationality` other than Philippine (PH, PHL, FILIPINO) is a foreign national; an unrecorded nationality raises nothing.
rules.applies_when: employee != null && has(employee.nationality) && employee.nationality != null && employee.nationality != "" && !(employee.nationality.upperAscii() in ["PH", "PHL", "FILIPINO", "PHILIPPINES", "PHILIPPINE"])

name: Written notice of an authorised-cause termination to the employee and DOLE

rules.description: Serve written notice of a termination for an authorised cause (labour-saving devices, redundancy, retrenchment, closure, disease) on the employee and on DOLE (RKS Form 5 / Establishment Report System).

rules.authority: the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the second tranche is a dated row of the same key from that day. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800, a dated row from 7 February 2026. the floor is mandatory — RA 6727 s.4 and Wage Order No. NCR-28 s.4 (the increase applies to “all minimum wage earners in the private sector within the region”) and s.6 (non-payment is dealt with under RA 6727 s.12); only an exemption the board approves on application (RA 6727 s.4(c)) lowers it, recorded as `company.facts.minimum_wage_exemption_approved` (default false: no approval, no exemption). A covered under-floor contract term is refused (validation MINIMUM_WAGE_FLOOR_CONTRACT) and a payslip below the floor of its period warns (MINIMUM_WAGE_FLOOR_PAYSLIP). a part-timer is refused too. The order’s daily rate is for normal working hours of at most eight a day and covers every minimum wage earner regardless of status (NCR-28 ss.3–4), and a worker on less than the normal hours is owed a proportion of it (DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.1 §L), so `wages.scale` multiplies a PART_TIME contract’s floor by its weekly hours over the full-time week of the person’s own factor (40 on a five-day week, 48 on a six-day one): the reference week is a recorded default, the orders naming none (20 hours on a five-day NCR-26 week: 695 × 261 ÷ 12 × 20 ÷ 40 = 7,558.13). The message quotes the floor on the person's own factor (₱755 × 261 ÷ 12 = 16,421.25 on a five-day week), not the 313-day basis. Signed NWPC board orders: additional private daily rates are II ₱500, CAR ₱505, IV-B ₱455; domestic monthly rates are I ₱6,700, II ₱6,500, III ₱6,500, IV-A ₱6,750, V ₱6,000, VI ₱6,500, XII ₱6,000, CAR ₱6,600, IV-B ₱7,000, XIII ₱6,500, X ₱6,500, BARMM ₱5,500, XI ₱6,500. The order PDFs are in this version’s sources. The private-sector exemption approval fact cannot displace a domestic floor; the inspected orders that address exemption expressly disallow it. Region V RBV-22 reaches ₱435 on 1 December 2025; Caraga RXIII-19 reaches ₱435 on 1 May 2025 and RXIII-20 sets ₱455 from 3 January 2026, ₱475 from 1 May 2026. Version design (the project’s accepted design for regional wage orders, coordinator design decision 2026-10-07): a sealed version is one national statutory regime — here the RR 29-2025 withholding and de minimis rules from 6 January 2026 — and the many regional wage orders (8, 15 and 30 Dec 2025; 1, 3, 8 and 16 Jan, 7 Feb, 13 Mar, 1, 8 and 16 Apr, 1 and 20 May, 1 Jun, 6 Aug, 1 and 26 Sep, 14 Oct and 1 Dec 2026) and the holiday proclamations are dated rows inside it, each key’s floor on a day being its first entry whose `from` is on or before the day (NWPC regional pages and signed orders read 2026-09-30). A settlement period spanning an order’s date takes the newer floor for the whole period (`from <= period.to`): for wages the stricter test, never an underpayment; for the minimum-wage-earner income-tax test (WTAX `person.mwe`) the same newer floor decides the whole period, so it can exempt days earned before the order — a recorded default whose exposure is nil in practice, a salary at or below the floor × 313 ÷ 12 being under the ₱250,000 annual zero bracket. A worksite whose predecessor rate is unread stays unseeded and refuses. VIII MANUFACTURING and OTHER_NONAGRI select the non-agriculture class (RB VIII-25 s.2 puts non-agriculture with retail of more than 10 workers); cottage/handicraft has no sector code of its own, so it is priced at the non-agriculture floor — a recorded default that never underpays. VIII domestic rows at the seven chartered cities select the chartered-city class (RBVIII-DW-06 s.1). BARMM/Cotabato City private rows follow BARMM-05 s.2: non-agriculture (manufacturing, other non-agriculture) and agriculture/retail. RA 9178 s.8 exempts a certified Barangay Micro Business Enterprise from the Minimum Wage Law, its employees keeping social security and health benefits, so `wages.applies_when` leaves a BMBE establishment (company fact `bmbe_certificate_of_authority`, default false) outside the private floor; a kasambahay stays covered by the domestic order. The contribution schemes do not read the fact. Wage Order No. IVA-22 s.2 (p.3 non-agriculture, p.5 agriculture, p.7 retail/service of 10 or fewer; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Wage-Order-No.-IVA-22_compressed.pdf) lists the City of Santo Tomas, Batangas among the component cities: non-agriculture ₱600 (`IV-A`), agriculture ₱525 (`IV-A-AGRI-COMPONENT-1ST`), retail/service of 10 or fewer ₱485 then ₱508 (`IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL`) — the same class as the City of Calamba, so `Batangas/Santo Tomas` carries Calamba's rows. Each key holds its dated floors newest first ({from, monthly}); the floor on a day is the first entry whose `from` is on or before it. Kasambahay floors are monthly as the domestic orders state them. Verified against the NWPC regional pages on 7 October 2026. NCR-27 (effective 25 July 2026, ₱780 from 20 January 2027) is not carried: NWPC marks it subject to litigation before RTC Pasig Branch 152 and RTC Navotas Branch 287; NCR-28 governs from 26 September 2026. NCR-28’s recitals (signed order, nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-28.pdf, read 2026-10-07) state that a Status Quo Ante Order (24 July 2026), a TRO and a writ of preliminary injunction mean "Wage Order No. NCR-27 never took effect": NCR-26 governs to 25 September 2026 and neither NCR-27 tranche (25 July 2026, 20 January 2027) is a floor; a lifted injunction is a new version from its date. RXIII-DW-06 s.1 (signed order read 2026-10-07) puts chartered cities, first-class and other municipalities on one row, ₱6,000 → ₱6,500, so Caraga has no other-municipality key.

name: Report the separated employee to PhilHealth (RF-1)

rules.description: Show the separated employee on the RF-1 remittance report.
rules.authority: PhilHealth, Reporting Your Employees (https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/partners/employers/report.php, checked 7 October 2026): "Indicate the names of separated employees in the RF-1 within 30 days from the date of separation".
rules.when: contract != null && contract.exit_facts != null && contract.effective_range.to != null

name: Transmit the maternity notice and advance the SSS maternity benefit

rules.description: Transmit the employee’s maternity notification to SSS and advance the full maternity benefit; claim reimbursement.
rules.authority: RA 11199 s.14-A as amended by RA 11210 s.5 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/86333): the employer transmits the notice to SSS, and "the full payment shall be advanced by the employer within thirty (30) days from the filing of the maternity leave application". Raised by a MATERNITY_LEAVE entry (`row.catalog_code`), due 30 days after it is filed (`today`).

name: Kasambahay written contract and barangay registration

rules.description: Execute the written employment contract with the kasambahay before service starts and register the kasambahay in the barangay Registry of Domestic Workers.
rules.authority: RA 10361 ss.11 and 17 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): the contract before the commencement of service; registration with the barangay of the employer’s residence. Recorded default: both due on the first day of service.
rules.applies_when: contract != null && has(contract.facts) && has(contract.facts.contract_terms) && contract.facts.contract_terms.exists(t, has(t.employment_type) && t.employment_type == "DOMESTIC")

name: Make the regularisation standards known to a probationary employee

rules.description: Make known at engagement the reasonable standards under which the probationary employee will qualify as regular; probation ends within six months of the actual start.
rules.authority: Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code Book VI Rule I ss.5(c), 6(a), (d) (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819): standards at the time of engagement; probation not beyond six months (Labor Code art.296).
rules.applies_when: contract != null && has(contract.facts) && has(contract.facts.contract_terms) && contract.facts.contract_terms.exists(t, has(t.employment_type) && t.employment_type == "PROBATION")

name: Register the employer with the Pag-IBIG Fund

rules.description: Submit the employer’s data to the Pag-IBIG Fund.
rules.authority: HDMF Circular 275 §C.4 (https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/document/pdf/circulars/provident/HDMF%20Circular%20275%20-%20Implementing%20Guidelines%20on%20Employer%20Registration%20Contribution%20and%20Remittance.pdf): employers submit their data "within thirty (30) days from the start of their business operations". Recorded default: counted from the entity’s effective start, else the month it was recorded.
rules.due: has(row.effective_range) && row.effective_range != null && has(row.effective_range.from) ? add_days(row.effective_range.from, 30) : add_days(period.from, 30)

name: Remit the protection-order support withheld

rules.description: Remit the support the protection order fixes, withheld from the respondent employee’s pay, directly to the woman and/or child it names.
rules.authority: RA 9262 s.8(g) (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/22128): the court orders a percentage of the respondent’s salary "to be withheld regularly by the respondent’s employer" and remitted directly; failure or delay without justifiable cause is indirect contempt. Raised by each PROTECTION_ORDER_SUPPORT entry (`row.catalog_code`). Recorded default: due on the entry’s pay day.

name: Compulsory retirement at sixty-five

rules.description: Retire the employee at sixty-five and pay at least the RA 7641 retirement pay (22.5 days a year of service, five years’ service).
rules.authority: Labor Code art.302 (RA 7641); DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 (https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Workers-Statutory-Monetary-Benefits-Handbook-2024-Edition.pdf) ch.15 §B: retirement at sixty or more "but not beyond 65 years". Raised once, on the sixty-fifth birthday.
rules.when: employee != null && has(employee.date_of_birth) && employee.date_of_birth != null && employee.date_of_birth != "" && add_years(employee.date_of_birth, 65.0) == today && contract != null && (contract.effective_range.to == null || contract.effective_range.to >= today)

name: Probation ends: regularise or end the employment

rules.description: Decide on regularisation: a probationary employee allowed to work after six months is regular.
rules.authority: Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code Book VI Rule I s.6(a), (d) (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819); Labor Code art.296: probation "shall not exceed six (6) months from the date the employee started working". Raised a month ahead, due the day before the six months end.
rules.when: contract != null && add_months(contract.effective_range.from, 5.0) == today && has(contract.facts) && has(contract.facts.contract_terms) && contract.facts.contract_terms.exists(t, has(t.employment_type) && t.employment_type == "PROBATION")

name: Five days’ notice to end a kasambahay’s employment

rules.description: Give the kasambahay five days’ notice of the end of an employment of undetermined duration.
rules.authority: RA 10361 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514) s.32: "If the duration of the domestic service is not determined … the employer or the domestic worker may give notice to end the working relationship five (5) days before the intended termination". Due five days before the last day.
rules.applies_when: contract != null && has(contract.facts) && has(contract.facts.contract_terms) && contract.facts.contract_terms.exists(t, has(t.employment_type) && t.employment_type == "DOMESTIC") && !(contract.exit_ground in ["DISMISSAL"])
rules.when: contract != null && contract.exit_facts != null && contract.effective_range.to != null

name: Twin-notice due process for a just-cause dismissal

rules.description: Serve the first written notice (charges, at least five calendar days to answer), hear the employee, then serve the written notice of decision.
rules.authority: Labor Code art.292(b): written notice of the causes and ample opportunity to be heard; DOLE Department Order 147-15 s.5.1(a): the first notice gives "at least five (5) calendar days" to explain. Due five days before the dismissal takes effect.
rules.when: contract != null && contract.exit_facts != null && contract.effective_range.to != null

name: Caregiver’s written employment contract

rules.description: Execute the caregiver’s employment contract, signed and notarised, before service starts; give the caregiver a copy.
rules.authority: RA 11965 s.5 (https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2023/ra_11965_2023.html): "An employment contract shall be executed … before the commencement of the service".
rules.applies_when: contract != null && has(contract.facts) && has(contract.facts.contract_terms) && contract.facts.contract_terms.exists(t, has(t.employment_type) && t.employment_type == "CAREGIVER")

name: Distribute the collected service charges

rules.description: Distribute the period’s service charges completely and equally among the covered workers (managerial employees excepted).
rules.authority: Labor Code art.96 as amended by RA 11360; Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819) Book III Rule VI s.4: the shares are paid "not less than once every two (2) weeks or twice a month at intervals not exceeding sixteen (16) days". Raised by each run of an entity that collects service charges; due by the run’s last day.

name: Record the work-connected contingency in the EC logbook

rules.description: Enter the sickness, injury or death in the Employees’ Compensation logbook.
rules.authority: PD 626 (Labor Code Book IV Title II) art.211 as relayed by the ECC (https://ecc.gov.ph/ecc-reminds-employers-to-comply-with-the-ec-logbook-template): "Entries in the logbook shall be made within five days from notice or knowledge of the occurrence of the contingency". Raised by a leave entry the employer marks work-connected (entry fact `work_connected`, customer input).

name: Report the work-connected contingency to SSS

rules.description: Report the work-connected sickness, injury or death to SSS for Employees’ Compensation.
rules.authority: PD 626 art.211 (ECC): "Within five days after entry in the logbook, the employer shall report to the System only those contingencies he deems to be work-connected".

name: Notify SSS of the employee’s confinement

rules.description: Notify SSS of the member’s confinement for the sickness benefit; advance the benefit on the regular paydays and claim reimbursement.

rules.description: RA 6727 s.4 and the regional wage orders (PAYROLL rule `minimum_wage`, NWPC): no employer pays less than the floor of the workplace (`terms.facts.wage_region`, else the entity’s `region`); a kasambahay’s is the domestic order’s monthly floor (RA 10361 s.24); a caregiver’s the regional floor (RA 11965 s.9); an apprentice not less than 75% (Labor Code art.61); a part-time contract on its hourly rate (`hours_per_day`). RA 9178 s.8: a certified BMBE is outside the minimum wage law; RA 6727 s.4(c): a board-approved exemption; RA 12063 s.13(a): a general EBET trainee is on an allowance. The floor is the daily rate; the contract’s rate is its daily rate for an 8-hour day. Read on the term’s own first day (`day`).

rules.message: rate below the regional minimum wage in force (RA 6727 s.4; a new wage order raises the floor from its effective date).
rules.description: RA 6727 s.4 and the regional wage orders (PAYROLL rule `minimum_wage`, NWPC): no employer pays less than the floor of the workplace (`terms.facts.wage_region`, else the entity’s `region`); a kasambahay’s is the domestic order’s monthly floor (RA 10361 s.24); a caregiver’s the regional floor (RA 11965 s.9); an apprentice not less than 75% (Labor Code art.61); a part-time contract on its hourly rate (`hours_per_day`). RA 9178 s.8: a certified BMBE is outside the minimum wage law; RA 6727 s.4(c): a board-approved exemption; RA 12063 s.13(a): a general EBET trainee is on an allowance. The floor is the daily rate; the contract’s rate is its daily rate for an 8-hour day. Read on the period’s last day, so a later wage order is caught.

name: A worker under eighteen past eight hours a day, forty a week, or at night

rules.when: employee.age != null && employee.age >= 15.0 && employee.age < 18.0 && (work.days.exists(d, d.worked_hours > 8.0 || hours_between(d.intervals, "22:00", "06:00") > 0.0) || work.days.exists(d, sum(work.days.filter(e, e.date >= d.date && e.date <= add_days(d.date, 6)).map(e, e.worked_hours)) > 40.0))
rules.message: a worker under eighteen worked more than eight hours a day, forty in a week, or between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. (RA 9231 s.12-A).
rules.description: RA 9231 s.12-A (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/1388): a child fifteen but below eighteen works at most eight hours a day and forty a week, never between ten in the evening and six in the morning; the week is any seven consecutive days of the period.

name: A kasambahay without eight hours’ daily rest

rules.when: terms.employment_type == "DOMESTIC" && work.days.exists(d, d.worked_hours > 16.0)
rules.message: a kasambahay worked more than sixteen hours in a day (RA 10361 s.20: eight hours’ daily rest).
rules.description: RA 10361 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514) s.20: "an aggregate daily rest period of eight (8) hours per day".

name: Seven consecutive days worked

rules.when: work.days.exists(d, size(work.days.filter(e, e.worked && e.date >= d.date && e.date <= add_days(d.date, 6))) >= 7)
rules.message: seven consecutive days worked: a rest of 24 consecutive hours is owed after six (Labor Code art.91; RA 10361 s.21 for a kasambahay).
rules.description: Labor Code art.91; Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819) Book III Rule III s.3: "a rest period of not less than twenty-four (24) consecutive hours after every six consecutive normal work days"; RA 10361 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514) s.21: a kasambahay at least 24 consecutive hours of rest a week. Rest-day work stays lawful in the art.92 cases; the warning asks HR to confirm one applied.

name: Wages paid less than twice a month

rules.when: (terms.employment_type == "DOMESTIC" && company.pay_frequency == "INTEGER_MONTHS") || (terms.employment_type != "DOMESTIC" && company.pay_frequency in ["MONTHLY", "INTEGER_MONTHS"])
rules.message: wages paid less than twice a month (Labor Code art.103: at least twice a month at intervals of 16 days or less; a kasambahay at least once a month).
rules.description: Labor Code art.103; Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819) Book III Rule VIII s.3(a): "not less than once every two (2) weeks or twice a month at intervals not exceeding sixteen (16) days"; RA 11965 s.10 for a caregiver; RA 10361 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514) s.25: a kasambahay "at least once a month". It covers managerial staff too: art.103 sits in Book III Title II (wages), outside the art.82 exclusion, which governs Title I (working conditions and rest periods) only, and Rule VIII s.1 reaches every private employee.

name: Probation beyond six months

rules.when: terms.employment_type == "PROBATION" && employment.start_date != "" && day >= add_months(employment.start_date, 6.0)
rules.message: Probation cannot run past six months from the first day of work (Labor Code art.296): an employee allowed to work after it is regular — record regular terms.
rules.description: Labor Code art.296; Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819) Book VI Rule I s.6(b), (d): probation "shall not exceed six (6) months reckoned from the date the employee actually started working"; one allowed to work after it is regular.

name: Paid as probationary past six months

rules.when: terms.employment_type == "PROBATION" && employment.start_date != "" && period.to >= add_months(employment.start_date, 6.0)
rules.message: still recorded as probationary six months after starting: the employee is regular (Labor Code art.296).
rules.description: Labor Code art.296; Omnibus Rules Book VI Rule I s.6(d).

name: Undertime offset against overtime

rules.when: work.days.exists(d, d.overtime_hours > 0.0 && d.worked && d.scheduled_hours > 0.0 && d.worked_hours < d.scheduled_hours + d.overtime_hours - 0.01)
rules.message: overtime approved on a day with undertime: undertime on one day may not offset overtime (Labor Code art.88).
rules.description: Labor Code art.88: "undertime work on any particular day shall not be offset by overtime work on any other day"; the warning flags approved overtime on a day the recorded hours do not reach the schedule plus that overtime.

name: A trainee contract names its EBET programme

rules.when: terms.employment_type in ["INTERN", "APPRENTICE"] && (!has(terms.facts.ebet_program) || (terms.employment_type == "APPRENTICE") != (terms.facts.ebet_program == "APPRENTICESHIP"))
rules.message: A trainee contract records its EBET programme (RA 12063 s.4): APPRENTICE for an apprenticeship, INTERN for general training or upskilling.
rules.description: RA 12063 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/98026) ss.4, 12–13: enterprise-based trainees are classified by registered programme; only an apprenticeship takes the 75% floor, a general trainee an allowance, an upskilling trainee the full wage. Customer input: `terms.facts.ebet_program`.

name: Not qualified for substituted filing

rules.when: ((period.month_key.endsWith("-12") && period.to == period.month_to) || (employment.exit_date != "" && employment.exit_date >= period.from && employment.exit_date <= period.to)) && has(employee.facts.previous_employer_taxable_compensation) && double(employee.facts.previous_employer_taxable_compensation) > 0.0
rules.message: compensation from another employer this year: not qualified for substituted filing (RR 2-98 s.2.83.4) — the employee files BIR Form 1700.
rules.description: RR 11-2018 (https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RR%20No.%2011-2018.pdf) s.2.83.4: substituted filing is for an employee with one employer in the year whose tax withheld equals the tax due; a previous employer’s compensation (employee fact) disqualifies.

name: Annual Establishment Report on Wages (NWPC)

rules.description: Submit the Annual Establishment Report on Wages: the verified itemised listing of the establishment’s rank-and-file labour component and their wages as of 31 December, one report per branch.
rules.authority: Labor Code art.124 as amended by RA 6727, as the NWPC FAQs state it: all private establishments (sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporations, cooperatives, GOCCs without original charter) submit annually a verified itemised listing of their labour component below the managerial level, with their salaries and wages; branches file separately. Labor Advisory 08-26 and the NWPC 2025 AERW FAQs (https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/2025-aerw-faqs/, read 2026-10-07): the CY2025 report, as of 31 December 2025, is submitted "within the period 15 May 2026 to 31 August 2026" through aerw.nwpc.dole.gov.ph. Raised by the entity’s daily calendar tick, not by a payroll run: the duty is the year’s whatever runs exist — from 1 December of the year covered through its due day, once a year (`repeat_key` the year covered), for an entity with an employment in force on the day (headcount above zero). Amounts and lists come from the year’s payslips (the alphalist exports, the 2316 figures).
rules.when: headcount > 0 && today >= (int(today.substring(5, 7)) == 12 ? today.substring(0, 4) : string(int(today.substring(0, 4)) - 1)) + "-12-01" && today <= string(int((int(today.substring(5, 7)) == 12 ? today.substring(0, 4) : string(int(today.substring(0, 4)) - 1))) + 1) + "-08-31"

name: Register the establishment with the DOLE regional office (Rule 1020)

rules.description: Register the establishment with the DOLE Regional Office having jurisdiction (OSH Standards Rule 1020), one registration per establishment location.
rules.authority: Occupational Safety and Health Standards (as amended, 1989; OSHC copy https://web.archive.org/web/2022id_/https://oshc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/OSH-Standard-2020.pdf, read 2026-10-07) Rule 1021: "Every employer ... shall register his business with the Regional Labor Office"; Rule 1022: each establishment in one single location is one registrable unit; Rule 1023(2): "New establishments shall register within thirty (30) days before operation." Rule 1024(2): free, valid for the life of the establishment, re-registered as new on a change of business name, location or ownership or on re-opening. RA 11058 and DO 198-18 keep the employer’s OSH duties under these Standards. Due on the entity’s first day of operations (its effective start, else the month it was recorded). A re-registration on a change of name, location or ownership is DOLE_ESTABLISHMENT_REREGISTRATION.
rules.due: has(row.effective_range) && row.effective_range != null && has(row.effective_range.from) ? add_days(row.effective_range.from, 0) : add_days(period.from, 0)

name: Workplace case kinds

rules.authority: The PH workplace cases the TASKS below answer: OSH Standards Rules 1053.01–1053.02 (work accidents, dangerous occurrences); DOLE DA 02-09 (flexible work arrangements); RA 11165 and DO 237-22 (telecommuting); DO 215-20 (suspension extended beyond six months); RA 8972 s.6 (solo parent’s flexible schedule). Case facts: `occurred_on`, `outcome` (DEATH, PERMANENT_TOTAL_DISABILITY), `starts_on` (customer input). NPC Circular 16-03 (personal data breach).

kinds.name: Work accident or occupational illness resulting in a disabling condition
Extension of a suspension of employment beyond six months (DO 215-20)
Solo parent’s flexible work schedule request (RA 8972 s.6)

name: Pay the SSS late-remittance penalty

rules.description: Pay the 2% a month penalty on the SSS contributions remitted after their due day, with the contributions.
rules.authority: RA 11199 s.22(a) (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/86333, read 2026-10-07): "the delinquent employer shall pay besides the contribution a penalty thereon of two percent (2%) per month from the date the contribution falls due until paid." Raised when the SSS remittance is recorded paid after its due day; due the day it was paid.
rules.when: row.state == "FULFILLED" && row.duty_code == "SSS_CONTRIBUTION_REMITTANCE" && has(row.fulfilled_on) && row.fulfilled_on != null && row.fulfilled_on > row.due_on

name: Pay the PhilHealth late-remittance interest

rules.description: Pay the missed PhilHealth premiums with interest compounded monthly at not less than 3% for employers.
rules.authority: RA 11223 s.9 (Universal Health Care Act; https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11223_2019.html, read 2026-10-07 — officialgazette.gov.ph answers 403; the E-Library copy was not located): employers "shall be required to pay all missed contributions with an interest, compounded monthly, of at least three percent (3%)"; RA 7875 s.16(v) as amended by RA 10606 lets PhilHealth fix interest or surcharges of not more than 3% a month. Raised when the PhilHealth remittance is recorded paid after its due day; due the day it was paid.
rules.when: row.state == "FULFILLED" && row.duty_code == "PHILHEALTH_PREMIUM_REMITTANCE" && has(row.fulfilled_on) && row.fulfilled_on != null && row.fulfilled_on > row.due_on

name: Pay the Pag-IBIG late-remittance penalty

rules.description: Pay the Pag-IBIG penalty of 1/10 of 1% a day of the amount due, from the day after the due day to full settlement.
rules.authority: HDMF Circular 275 §E (https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/document/pdf/circulars/provident/HDMF%20Circular%20275%20-%20Implementing%20Guidelines%20on%20Employer%20Registration%20Contribution%20and%20Remittance.pdf, read 2026-10-07): the employer "shall be charged a penalty equivalent to 1/10 of 1% per day of delay of the amount due starting on the first day immediately following the due date until the date of full settlement", the Board’s rate under RA 9679 s.13 (power to "fix and impose interest and penalties upon unpaid contributions"); RA 9679 s.23 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/19155) caps the statutory penalty at 3% a month. Raised when the Pag-IBIG remittance is recorded paid after its due day; due the day it was paid.
rules.when: row.state == "FULFILLED" && row.duty_code == "HDMF_CONTRIBUTION_REMITTANCE" && has(row.fulfilled_on) && row.fulfilled_on != null && row.fulfilled_on > row.due_on

name: Employer’s Work Accident/Illness Report (WAIR) to the DOLE regional office

rules.description: Report the work accident or occupational illness that resulted in a disabling condition to the DOLE regional office (form DOLE/BWC/HSD-IP-6, in duplicate, a copy to the employee).
rules.authority: OSH Standards Rule 1053.01(1) (https://web.archive.org/web/2022id_/https://oshc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/OSH-Standard-2020.pdf, read 2026-10-07): the formal report "shall be submitted by the employer on or before the 20th day of the month following the date of occurrence of the accident or when the illness is established"; DO 198-18 s.17 and Labor Advisory 04-19 ¶5(a) (both in the same OSHC edition) keep the WAIR. Raised when a WORK_ACCIDENT case (a disabling injury or illness) is opened; the occurrence is `facts.occurred_on`, else the opening day.
rules.when: row.kind == "WORK_ACCIDENT"
rules.due: add_days(month_end((has(row.facts) && row.facts != null && has(row.facts.occurred_on) && row.facts.occurred_on != "" ? row.facts.occurred_on : row.opened_on)), 20)

name: Notify the DOLE regional office of a death or permanent total disability within 24 hours

rules.description: Notify the DOLE regional office within 24 hours by the fastest available means when a work accident or illness results in death or permanent total disability, besides the WAIR.
rules.authority: OSH Standards Rule 1053.01(2) (https://web.archive.org/web/2022id_/https://oshc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/OSH-Standard-2020.pdf, read 2026-10-07): "the employer ... shall initially notify the Regional Labor Office ... within twenty four (24) hours after occurrence using the fastest available means of communication"; Labor Advisory 04-19: serious injuries and deaths are notified immediately. Raised when a WORK_ACCIDENT case records `facts.outcome` DEATH or PERMANENT_TOTAL_DISABILITY; due the day after the occurrence.
rules.when: row.kind == "WORK_ACCIDENT" && has(row.facts) && row.facts != null && has(row.facts.outcome) && row.facts.outcome in ["DEATH", "PERMANENT_TOTAL_DISABILITY"]
rules.due: add_days((has(row.facts) && row.facts != null && has(row.facts.occurred_on) && row.facts.occurred_on != "" ? row.facts.occurred_on : row.opened_on), 1)

name: Report a dangerous occurrence to the DOLE regional office

rules.description: Investigate and report the dangerous occurrence (boiler or pressure-vessel explosion, bursting wheel, crane collapse, a fire or electrical failure stopping work for 24 hours or more) to the DOLE regional office on form DOLE/BWC/HSD-IP-6.
rules.authority: OSH Standards Rule 1053.02 (https://web.archive.org/web/2022id_/https://oshc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/OSH-Standard-2020.pdf, read 2026-10-07): a dangerous occurrence "shall be investigated and reported by the employer upon occurrence". Raised when a DANGEROUS_OCCURRENCE case is opened; due on the occurrence day.
rules.when: row.kind == "DANGEROUS_OCCURRENCE"
rules.due: add_days((has(row.facts) && row.facts != null && has(row.facts.occurred_on) && row.facts.occurred_on != "" ? row.facts.occurred_on : row.opened_on), 0)

name: Annual Work Accident/Illness Exposure Data Report (AEDR)

rules.description: Submit the Annual Work Accident/Illness Exposure Data Report (form DOLE/BWC/HSD-IP-6b), with or without accident cases, to the Bureau of Working Conditions, a copy to the regional office.
rules.authority: OSH Standards Rule 1054(2) (https://web.archive.org/web/2022id_/https://oshc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/OSH-Standard-2020.pdf, read 2026-10-07): "on or before the 30th day of the month following the end of each calendar year"; Labor Advisory 04-19 ¶5(b): "(with or without accident cases) on or before January 30 following the covered year". Raised by the entity’s daily calendar tick, not by a payroll run: the duty is the year’s whatever runs exist — from 1 December of the year covered through its due day, once a year (`repeat_key` the year covered), for an entity with an employment in force on the day (headcount above zero). Amounts and lists come from the year’s payslips (the alphalist exports, the 2316 figures).
rules.when: headcount > 0 && today >= (int(today.substring(5, 7)) == 12 ? today.substring(0, 4) : string(int(today.substring(0, 4)) - 1)) + "-12-01" && today <= string(int((int(today.substring(5, 7)) == 12 ? today.substring(0, 4) : string(int(today.substring(0, 4)) - 1))) + 1) + "-01-30"

name: Annual Medical Report (AMR) to the DOLE regional office

rules.description: Submit the Annual Medical Report (form DOLE/BWC/HSD/OH-47) to the DOLE regional office, a copy to the Bureau of Working Conditions.
rules.authority: OSH Standards Rule 1965.01(4) (https://web.archive.org/web/2022id_/https://oshc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/OSH-Standard-2020.pdf, read 2026-10-07): the employer submits the annual medical report "on or before the last day of March of the year following the covered period"; Labor Advisory 04-19 ¶5(c): "on or before March 31 following the covered year"; DO 198-18 s.17 lists the AMR among the OSH reports. Raised by the entity’s daily calendar tick, not by a payroll run: the duty is the year’s whatever runs exist — from 1 December of the year covered through its due day, once a year (`repeat_key` the year covered), for an entity with an employment in force on the day (headcount above zero). Amounts and lists come from the year’s payslips (the alphalist exports, the 2316 figures).
rules.when: headcount > 0 && today >= (int(today.substring(5, 7)) == 12 ? today.substring(0, 4) : string(int(today.substring(0, 4)) - 1)) + "-12-01" && today <= string(int((int(today.substring(5, 7)) == 12 ? today.substring(0, 4) : string(int(today.substring(0, 4)) - 1))) + 1) + "-03-31"

name: Notify the DOLE regional office before a flexible work arrangement starts

rules.description: Notify the DOLE regional office with jurisdiction over the workplace, on the DA 02-09 report form, of the flexible work arrangement (compressed workweek, reduced workdays, rotation, forced leave, broken-time or flexi-holiday schedule) before it is implemented.
rules.authority: DOLE Department Advisory 02-09 Part V (https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/http://www.bwc.dole.gov.ph/images/Issuances/DepartmentAdvisory/DA_02_09_2.pdf, read 2026-10-07): "Prior to its implementation, the employer shall notify the Department through the Regional Office which has jurisdiction over the workplace, of the adoption of any of the above flexible work arrangements"; Department Advisory 04-10 Part V repeats it. Raised when a FLEXIBLE_WORK_ARRANGEMENT case is opened; due the day before `facts.starts_on`, else before the opening day.
rules.when: row.kind == "FLEXIBLE_WORK_ARRANGEMENT"
rules.due: add_days((has(row.facts) && row.facts != null && has(row.facts.starts_on) && row.facts.starts_on != "" ? row.facts.starts_on : row.opened_on), -1)

name: Notify the DOLE of a telecommuting program through the Establishment Report System

rules.description: Notify the DOLE of the telecommuting program through the Establishment Report System (reports.dole.gov.ph), listing every branch implementing it; keep the proof of voluntary adoption three years.
rules.authority: DO 237-22 (Revised IRR of RA 11165) s.10 (https://web.archive.org/web/2023id_/https://bwc.dole.gov.ph/images/Issuances/DepartmentOrder/DO_237_22.pdf, read 2026-10-07; supersedes DO 202-19): "The employer shall notify the DOLE of the implementation of telecommuting through the Establishment Report System". The rule names no period: a recorded default due on the program’s start (`facts.starts_on`, else the opening day). Raised when a TELECOMMUTING_PROGRAM case is opened.
rules.when: row.kind == "TELECOMMUTING_PROGRAM"
rules.due: add_days((has(row.facts) && row.facts != null && has(row.facts.starts_on) && row.facts.starts_on != "" ? row.facts.starts_on : row.opened_on), 0)

name: Report the extension of a suspension of employment to the DOLE ten days before

rules.description: Report to the DOLE regional office the extension of the suspension of employment beyond six months (declared war, pandemic or similar national emergency), ten days before it takes effect.
rules.authority: Omnibus Rules Book VI Rule I s.12 as amended by DO 215-20 (https://web.archive.org/web/2021id_/https://www.dole.gov.ph/php_assets/uploads/2020/10/DO-215-20-Rule-Amending-Section-12-of-Rule-I-Rules-Implementing-Book-VI-of-the-Labor-Code-on-Suspension-of-Employment-Relationship.pdf, read 2026-10-07): "the employer shall report to the Department of Labor and Employment, through the Regional Offices, the extension of suspension of employment ten (10) days prior to the effectivity thereof subject to inspection". A suspension of operations within six months (Labor Code art.301) has no DOLE report in the instruments read. Raised when a SUSPENSION_EXTENSION case is opened; the extension’s first day is `facts.starts_on`, else the opening day.
rules.when: row.kind == "SUSPENSION_EXTENSION"
rules.due: add_days((has(row.facts) && row.facts != null && has(row.facts.starts_on) && row.facts.starts_on != "" ? row.facts.starts_on : row.opened_on), -10)

name: Provide the solo parent’s flexible work schedule

rules.description: Give the solo parent employee a flexible work schedule (arrival and departure varied around the core hours), unless the DOLE has exempted the employer on meritorious grounds; solo parents have priority for a telecommuting program, and no term or condition may discriminate on account of the status.
rules.authority: RA 8972 s.6 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/3532, read 2026-10-07): "The employer shall provide for a flexible working schedule for solo parents: Provided, That the same shall not affect individual and company productivity: Provided, further, That any employer may request exemption ... from the DOLE"; s.3(c) as amended by RA 11861 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/95472) defines the schedule; s.7 as amended by RA 11861 s.6 forbids discrimination and gives solo parents priority for telecommuting. The Act names no period: a recorded default due on the request day. Raised when a SOLO_PARENT_FLEXIBLE_SCHEDULE case is opened (opened_on = the request).
rules.when: row.kind == "SOLO_PARENT_FLEXIBLE_SCHEDULE"

name: Wages in tokens or vouchers

rules.when: (has(terms.facts.wage_payment_medium) ? terms.facts.wage_payment_medium : "") == "TOKEN_OR_VOUCHER"
rules.message: wages must be paid in legal tender: tokens, promissory notes, vouchers and coupons are absolutely prohibited, even at the employee’s request (Labor Code art.102; Omnibus Rules Book III Rule VIII s.1).
rules.description: Labor Code art.102; Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819, read 2026-10-07) Book III Rule VIII s.1: "the use of tokens, promissory notes, vouchers, coupons, or any other form alleged to represent legal tender is absolutely prohibited even when expressly requested by the employee". The medium is the contract-term fact `wage_payment_medium` (customer input; unrecorded = not checked).

name: Cheque, bank or e-wallet payment without the Rule VIII s.2 conditions

rules.when: (has(terms.facts.wage_payment_medium) ? terms.facts.wage_payment_medium : "") in ["CHEQUE", "BANK_TRANSFER", "E_WALLET"] && !(has(company.facts.wage_payment_conditions_met) && company.facts.wage_payment_conditions_met)
rules.message: wages by cheque, bank or e-wallet need the Rule VIII s.2 conditions: customary or under a CBA, or an encashment facility within 1 km, no benefit to the employer, paid time to withdraw and the employee’s written consent (Omnibus Rules Book III Rule VIII s.2).
rules.description: Labor Code art.102; Omnibus Rules (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819, read 2026-10-07) Book III Rule VIII s.2: payment "by bank checks, postal checks or money orders is allowed where such manner of wage payment is customary ..., where it is so stipulated in a collective agreement, or where all of the following conditions are met" — (a) a bank or other encashment facility within one kilometre of the workplace, (b) no pecuniary benefit to the employer, (c) reasonable time during banking hours to withdraw, counted as hours worked, (d) the employees’ written consent absent a CBA. A bank transfer or e-wallet is read as the same kind of non-cash medium (a recorded reading: the Rule names cheques and money orders); the conditions are the entity fact `wage_payment_conditions_met` (customer input, one per establishment; owner ruling 2026-10-07). A warning, since a CBA or custom also suffices. Cash and bank transfer both stay allowed; the warning only asks for the establishment’s s.2 conditions.

name: Wages paid in a bar, club or gaming place

rules.when: (has(terms.facts.wage_payment_place) ? terms.facts.wage_payment_place : "") == "BAR_CLUB_OR_GAMING_PLACE" && !(has(terms.facts.employed_at_payment_place) && terms.facts.employed_at_payment_place)
rules.message: wages may not be paid in a bar, night or day club, drinking establishment, massage clinic, dance hall or gaming place unless the employee works there (Omnibus Rules Book III Rule VIII s.4(d)).
rules.description: Labor Code art.104; Omnibus Rules (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819, read 2026-10-07) Book III Rule VIII s.4: "the place of payment shall be at or near the place of undertaking"; elsewhere only (a) when peace and order or a calamity prevents payment there, (b) with free transport both ways, (c) in analogous circumstances — the collecting time being hours worked — and (d) "No employer shall pay his employees in any bar, night or day club, drinking establishment, massage clinic, dance hall, or other similar places or in places where games are played with stakes ... except in the case of persons employed in said places". The place is the term fact `wage_payment_place` and the exception `employed_at_payment_place` (customer input). The permitted elsewhere-cases (a)–(c) pass; (d) is refused.

name: BIR 1604-C alphalist — Schedule 1 (employees other than MWEs)

rules.authority: RR 2-98 s.2.79(B)(5)(b) and s.2.83.2 as amended by RR 11-2018 (https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RR%20No.%2011-2018.pdf, read 2026-10-07): the annualised computation of each employee "shall be reflected by the employer at the alphabetical list of employees required to be attached to BIR Form No. 1604C. The list shall be submitted in electronic form"; columns per the BIR 1604-C Alphalist Format (Schedule 1 — employees other than MWEs; Schedule 2 — minimum wage earners; https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/1604C%20Alphalist%20Format%20-%20final.pdf, read 2026-10-07). Export the year’s runs (January to December). Read from the selected runs’ payslips: pay by its WTAX part (the version’s own catalogue), the employee shares of SSS, MPF, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG and union dues, the WTAX withheld (December or the exit slip carries the year-end adjustment). Seq. No. is the row index. Names: the employee facts `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name` when declared; else `name` read as “Last, First Middle” when it has a comma, else “First … Middle Last”, a surname keeping its particles (DE, DEL, DELA, DELOS, DE LA, DE LOS, DE LAS, SAN, STA, STO, SANTA, SANTO, VDA, DI, DA, DOS — e.g. DELA GENTE, DE LOS REYES) and the word before it read as the middle name (declare the parts when a second given name would be misread). Schedule 1 reports an employee under “Salaries and Other Forms of Compensation (P250,000 & below)” only when the taxable compensation of the exported runs is ₱250,000 or less and no tax was withheld on it (an employee taxed in the year is a taxable row, 7g–7j). Recorded defaults: the 13th-month column holds the ₱90,000 pool (13th month, bonuses and de minimis excess, at the ceilings the version prices), the overtime-meal allowance and monetised leave are reported as de minimis whole (their daily-floor and daily-rate ceilings are not in the export context); only the previous employer’s taxable compensation and tax (employee facts from its 2316) fill the previous-employer columns, its TIN and breakdown being HR’s; the PERA credit is 0; Substituted Filing is Yes for an employee with no previous employer who is still employed at year end (the spouse requisite is the employee’s). An MWE is an employee every one of whose salary slips carries the MWE_STATUS scheme line with a base (a zero-charge marker the WTAX test sets; it shows on no payslip).
rules.when: totals.gross > 0.0 && !(size(slips.filter(s, (has(s.statutory.MWE_STATUS) && s.statutory.MWE_STATUS.base > 0.0))) > 0 && size(slips.filter(s, has(s.lines.BASIC) && !(has(s.statutory.MWE_STATUS) && s.statutory.MWE_STATUS.base > 0.0))) == 0)

name: BIR 1604-C alphalist — Schedule 2 (minimum wage earners)

rules.authority: RR 2-98 s.2.79(B)(5)(b) and s.2.83.2 as amended by RR 11-2018 (https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RR%20No.%2011-2018.pdf, read 2026-10-07): the annualised computation of each employee "shall be reflected by the employer at the alphabetical list of employees required to be attached to BIR Form No. 1604C. The list shall be submitted in electronic form"; columns per the BIR 1604-C Alphalist Format (Schedule 1 — employees other than MWEs; Schedule 2 — minimum wage earners; https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/1604C%20Alphalist%20Format%20-%20final.pdf, read 2026-10-07). Export the year’s runs (January to December). Read from the selected runs’ payslips: pay by its WTAX part (the version’s own catalogue), the employee shares of SSS, MPF, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG and union dues, the WTAX withheld (December or the exit slip carries the year-end adjustment). Seq. No. is the row index. Names: the employee facts `last_name`, `first_name`, `middle_name` when declared; else `name` read as “Last, First Middle” when it has a comma, else “First … Middle Last”, a surname keeping its particles (DE, DEL, DELA, DELOS, DE LA, DE LOS, DE LAS, SAN, STA, STO, SANTA, SANTO, VDA, DI, DA, DOS — e.g. DELA GENTE, DE LOS REYES) and the word before it read as the middle name (declare the parts when a second given name would be misread). Schedule 1 reports an employee under “Salaries and Other Forms of Compensation (P250,000 & below)” only when the taxable compensation of the exported runs is ₱250,000 or less and no tax was withheld on it (an employee taxed in the year is a taxable row, 7g–7j). Recorded defaults: the 13th-month column holds the ₱90,000 pool (13th month, bonuses and de minimis excess, at the ceilings the version prices), the overtime-meal allowance and monetised leave are reported as de minimis whole (their daily-floor and daily-rate ceilings are not in the export context); only the previous employer’s taxable compensation and tax (employee facts from its 2316) fill the previous-employer columns, its TIN and breakdown being HR’s; the PERA credit is 0; Substituted Filing is Yes for an employee with no previous employer who is still employed at year end (the spouse requisite is the employee’s). An MWE is an employee every one of whose salary slips carries the MWE_STATUS scheme line with a base (a zero-charge marker the WTAX test sets; it shows on no payslip).

name: Record retention after exit

rules.authority: NIRC s.235 as amended by RA 11976 (Ease of Paying Taxes Act) s.33 (https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_11976_2024.html, read 2026-10-07; officialgazette.gov.ph answers 403): books of accounts and other accounting records "shall be preserved by them for a period of five (5) years reckoned from the day following the deadline in filing a return ... for the taxable year when the last entry was made"; the exit year’s last payroll entry falls in the employer’s return for that year, due 15 April of the next year for a calendar-year taxpayer, so the records are kept to 15 April of the exit year + 6 — recorded as 31 December of the exit year + 6, which also covers a fiscal year ending by the following June. Longer than the Labor Code’s three years: Omnibus Rules Book III Rule X s.12 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819): employment records "preserved for at least three (3) years from the date of the last entry", and Labor Code art.306 (money claims prescribe in three years). RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act) s.11(e) (https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10173_2012.html; privacy.gov.ph answers 403): personal information is "Retained only for as long as necessary for the fulfillment of the purposes for which the data was obtained or for the establishment, exercise or defense of legal claims ... or as provided by law" — so it is disposed of (anonymised) after.

name: Anonymise a former employee’s personal data after retention

rules.description: Once the statutory retention ends (31 December of the exit year + 6: NIRC s.235 five years from the return deadline, longer than the Labor Code’s three years), stop retaining the former employee’s personal data: anonymise the profile (employment_profile anonymise, which record_retention releases on the same day) unless a legal claim or another law still needs it. Raised at the exit; due that day.

rules.when: contract != null && contract.effective_range.to != null

name: Seventh consecutive day worked

rules.when: day.worked && week.worked_days >= 7
rules.message: the seventh consecutive day worked: a rest of 24 consecutive hours is owed after six (Labor Code art.91; RA 10361 s.21 for a kasambahay). Confirm an art.92 case applies.
rules.description: Labor Code art.91; Omnibus Rules (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819, read 2026-10-07) Book III Rule III s.3: "a rest period of not less than twenty-four (24) consecutive hours after every six consecutive normal work days"; RA 10361 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514) s.21. A warning: rest-day work is lawful in the art.92 cases (emergencies, urgent work, perishable goods, …), so the record stays.

name: A minor over the daily or weekly hours

rules.when: (employee.age != null && employee.age >= 15.0 && employee.age < 18.0 && (day.worked_hours > 8.0 || week.worked_hours > 40.0)) || (employee.age != null && employee.age >= 0.0 && employee.age < 15.0 && (day.worked_hours > 4.0 || week.worked_hours > 20.0))
rules.message: a worker under eighteen over the RA 9231 hours: fifteen to seventeen at most eight a day and forty a week; under fifteen at most four a day and twenty a week (RA 7610 s.12-A as amended by RA 9231).
rules.description: RA 7610 s.12-A as amended by RA 9231 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/1388, read 2026-10-07): a child below fifteen works at most twenty hours a week and four a day; a child fifteen to below eighteen at most eight hours a day and forty a week. A warning, not a refusal: the Act forbids the work, not its record — the actual hours are kept and HR corrects the schedule.

name: A minor working at night

rules.when: (employee.age != null && employee.age >= 15.0 && employee.age < 18.0 && hours_between(day.intervals, "22:00", "06:00") > 0.0) || (employee.age != null && employee.age >= 0.0 && employee.age < 15.0 && hours_between(day.intervals, "20:00", "06:00") > 0.0)
rules.message: a worker under eighteen worked at night: fifteen to seventeen never between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m., under fifteen never between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m. (RA 7610 s.12-A as amended by RA 9231).
rules.description: RA 7610 s.12-A as amended by RA 9231 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/1388, read 2026-10-07): no child below fifteen works between eight in the evening and six in the morning, nor one fifteen to below eighteen between ten in the evening and six in the morning. A warning: the record of the hours is kept.

name: A kasambahay without eight hours’ daily rest

rules.when: terms.employment_type == "DOMESTIC" && day.worked_hours > 16.0
rules.message: a kasambahay worked more than sixteen hours in a day: an aggregate daily rest of eight hours is owed (RA 10361 s.20).
rules.description: RA 10361 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514, read 2026-10-07) s.20: "an aggregate daily rest period of eight (8) hours per day". A warning.

name: A planned day over twelve hours

rules.when: day.scheduled_hours > 12.0
rules.message: the day’s shift plans more than twelve hours: a compressed workweek may lengthen the normal day past eight hours but not beyond twelve (DOLE DA 02-04; DA 02-09 Part III.1).
rules.description: DOLE Department Advisory 02-09 Part III.1 (https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/http://www.bwc.dole.gov.ph/images/Issuances/DepartmentAdvisory/DA_02_09_2.pdf, read 2026-10-07), restating DA 02-04: under a compressed workweek "the normal workday is increased to more than eight hours but not to exceed twelve hours, without corresponding overtime premium"; Labor Code art.83: the normal day is eight hours. A planned shift over twelve hours is outside any approved CWW; work beyond eight is overtime (art.87). A warning: the hours may be lawful overtime.

name: Re-register the establishment with the DOLE regional office (Rule 1024(2))

rules.description: Re-register the establishment with the DOLE regional office as if it were new: its business name, its location (the entity’s region) or its registration (read as a change of ownership) changed.
rules.authority: OSH Standards Rule 1024(2) (https://web.archive.org/web/2022id_/https://oshc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/OSH-Standard-2020.pdf, read 2026-10-07): registration is valid for the life of the establishment "except when any of the following conditions exists, in which case, re-registration as if it were a new establishment is required: a. change in business name, b. change in location, c. change in ownership, or d. re-opening after previous closing". Raised when an entity update changes its `name`, `region` or `registration_number` (`row.before` holds the prior value; a new registration number is read as the change of ownership — recorded reading); due on the change day, since a new establishment registers before it operates (Rule 1023(2)). A re-opening is a new entity, raised by DOLE_ESTABLISHMENT_REGISTRATION.
rules.when: has(row.before) && row.before != null && ("name" in row.before || "region" in row.before || "registration_number" in row.before)

name: Night work around childbirth

rules.when: employee.gender == "FEMALE" && hours_between(day.intervals, "00:00", "05:00") > 0.0 && (employee.children.exists(c, has(c.estimated_delivery_date) && c.estimated_delivery_date != "" && (!has(c.child_birthdate) || c.child_birthdate == "") && day.date >= add_days(c.estimated_delivery_date, -112)) || employee.children.exists(c, has(c.child_birthdate) && c.child_birthdate != "" && day.date >= add_days(c.child_birthdate, -112) && day.date <= add_days(c.child_birthdate, 112)) || (has(employee.facts.night_work_alternative_until) && employee.facts.night_work_alternative_until != "" && day.date <= employee.facts.night_work_alternative_until))
rules.message: a woman worker around childbirth worked at night (midnight to 5 a.m.): an alternative to night work must be available for at least sixteen weeks divided before and after childbirth, and for a medically certified additional period (Labor Code art.158 as inserted by RA 10151).
rules.description: Labor Code art.158 as inserted by RA 10151 s.4 (https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2011/ra_10151_2011.html, read 2026-10-07; officialgazette.gov.ph answers 403): "measures shall be taken to ensure that an alternative to night work is available to women workers who would otherwise be called upon to perform such work: (a) Before and after childbirth, for a period of at least sixteen (16) weeks, which shall be divided between the time before and after childbirth; (b) For additional periods, in respect of which a medical certificate is produced". Art.154: night work is a period of not less than seven consecutive hours "including the interval from midnight to five o'clock in the morning" — the rule reads that interval, the statutory core (the DOLE-fixed window is not read). The Act lets the sixteen weeks be divided either way, so the warning covers sixteen weeks before the expected delivery (`children[].estimated_delivery_date`) through sixteen weeks after the birth (`child_birthdate`) — a recorded default that never misses a split; the certified additional period is the employee fact `night_work_alternative_until`. A warning: the article requires an alternative to be offered, not that the hours go unrecorded.

name: Designate the Data Protection Officer

rules.description: Designate the individual accountable for the entity’s compliance with the Data Privacy Act — the Data Protection Officer — and make the designation known.
rules.authority: RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act) s.21(b) (https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10173_2012.html, read 2026-10-07; privacy.gov.ph answers 403): the personal information controller "shall designate an individual or individuals who are accountable for the organization’s compliance with this Act"; payroll processes sensitive personal information (s.3(l): government-issued numbers, tax returns, health). Due on the entity’s first day of operations (recorded default: the Act names no period).

name: Register the data processing systems and DPO with the NPC

rules.description: Register the payroll data processing system and the DPO with the National Privacy Commission (mandatory at 250 or more employees, or when processing sensitive personal information of 1,000 or more individuals); renew the one-year certificate within the 30 days before it expires.
rules.authority: NPC Circular 2022-04 (https://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/https://privacy.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Circular-2022-04-1.pdf, read 2026-10-07) s.5: a PIC "that employs two hundred fifty (250) or more persons, or those processing sensitive personal information of one thousand (1,000) or more individuals ... shall register all Data Processing Systems"; s.7: register "within twenty (20) days from the commencement of such system or the effectivity date of such appointment"; s.18: renewal 30 days before the one-year validity ends (NPC_REGISTRATION_RENEWAL, yearly); s.6: an entity outside s.5 files a sworn declaration instead. Raised at the entity’s creation when its headcount is 250 or more, or the entity fact `processes_sensitive_pi_1000` holds (customer input: the count of data subjects whose sensitive personal information is processed); due twenty days from its start.

name: Notify the NPC and the data subjects of a personal data breach within 72 hours

rules.description: Notify the National Privacy Commission and the affected data subjects within 72 hours of knowing of (or reasonably believing in) a notifiable personal data breach — sensitive personal information or information enabling identity fraud (SSS, PhilHealth, TIN numbers, financial data) acquired by an unauthorised person with a real risk of serious harm; the full report follows within five days when the breach involves 100 or more data subjects or sensitive information.
rules.authority: NPC Circular 16-03 (https://web.archive.org/web/2018id_/http://privacy.gov.ph:80/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/sgd-npc-circular-16-03-personal-data-breach-management.pdf, read 2026-10-07) s.11 (when notification is required), s.17(A): "The Commission shall be notified within seventy-two (72) hours upon knowledge of or the reasonable belief ... that a personal data breach has occurred", s.17(C): the full report "within five (5) days"; s.18(A): data subjects "within seventy-two (72) hours"; RA 10173 s.20(f). Raised when a PERSONAL_DATA_BREACH case is opened (opened_on = the day of knowledge); due three days after.
rules.when: row.kind == "PERSONAL_DATA_BREACH"

name: Submit the full personal data breach report to the NPC

rules.description: Submit the full report of the personal data breach to the NPC within five days of the notification, unless the Commission grants more time.
rules.authority: NPC Circular 16-03 (https://web.archive.org/web/2018id_/http://privacy.gov.ph:80/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/sgd-npc-circular-16-03-personal-data-breach-management.pdf, read 2026-10-07) s.17(C): "The full report of the personal data breach must be submitted within five (5) days, unless the personal information controller is granted additional time by the Commission". Raised with the notification; due eight days after the day of knowledge (three for the notice, five for the report — recorded default).
rules.when: row.kind == "PERSONAL_DATA_BREACH"
